$comment: The machine-readable twin of E2E-MANUAL.md. One entry per phase, one entry per checkbox, in document order. Keep in step with the prose: check-e2e-flows.mjs fails if the phase or step counts disagree, or if a step's kind is missing. 'kind' is 'auto' (Playwright can assert it), 'human' (a person must judge it), or 'auto+human' (assert the state, judge the look).

longClip.why: seek and resume need a clip longer than the position sought; the demo clips are three seconds
longClip.command: ffmpeg -hide_banner -loglevel error -y -f lavfi -i "testsrc2=size=640x360:rate=15:duration=180" -f lavfi -i "sine=frequency=440:duration=180" -c:v libx264 -preset ultrafast -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:a aac -shortest /tmp/astraeus-e2e/long.mp4

ocrClip.why: to exercise the image-subtitle OCR and burn paths, the committed VobSub fixture has to be muxed onto a video track
ocrClip.command: ffmpeg -hide_banner -loglevel error -y -f lavfi -i "color=c=0x202020:s=640x360:r=15" -t 6 -i internal/subtitles/testdata/vobsub-caption.mkv -map 0:v -map 1:s -c:v libx264 -preset ultrafast -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:s copy /tmp/astraeus-e2e/ocr.mkv

phases.title: Playback, and the decision behind it

steps.expect: a direct-playable H.264 clip negotiates direct_play and starts
steps.assert: capture POST playback and assert the mode and reasons
steps.responseShape: mode is top-level; reasons, target codecs and the chosen audio stream are inside decision; media_info is beside them

steps.expect: an HEVC entity transcodes and a quality control appears; a direct-play entity has none
steps.assert: assert presence for the transcode and absence for direct play
steps.manifest: the client manifest needs supports_hls:true or the server answers not_deliverable instead of transcoding

steps.expect: choosing 'Up to Np' re-negotiates with preferred_height and no max_height
steps.assert: the request fields and a ladder topped at the choice

steps.expect: both tracks are offered and the file's default is current
steps.assert: the menu has as many entries as the server reports, and switching re-negotiates with the matching index

steps.expect: a segmented play loads hls.js lazily; direct play does not
steps.assert: window.Hls is undefined before and defined after

steps.expect: the bar auto-hides while playing and returns on pointer movement
steps.why: a judgement about feel, and three-second clips end during the wait

steps.expect: Space and the bar control both toggle playback and the glyph follows
steps.assert: paused flips and the control state changes

steps.expect: seeking re-negotiates at the offset rather than buffering from zero
steps.assert: the new request carries an offset near where the seek landed

steps.expect: the volume choice survives a reload
steps.assert: the stored value survives page.reload()

steps.expect: the player container goes fullscreen, not the bare video, and the control follows
steps.assert: document.fullscreenElement is the player container

steps.expect: Off plus every deliverable track; choosing one attaches a track with real cues
steps.assert: a <track> is attached, its TextTrack produces cues, Off disables them

steps.expect: the caption changes at the cue boundary and the fixture's ampersands render as text
steps.why: a person can see that & did not become & on screen

steps.expect: with tesseract, the image track is offered without '(burned in)' and choosing it makes no playback request
steps.assert: no playback request, and the cue text is the fixture's caption

steps.expect: without tesseract the same track is '(burned in)' and choosing it re-negotiates with burn_subtitle_index
steps.assert: the request carries burn_subtitle_index and the decision carries burned_subtitle_index

steps.assert: read the transport's source clock, not the element's

phases.title: The API as a client sees it

steps.expect: a scan returns 200 and a second scan does not change the entity count
steps.assert: status and a stable count

steps.expect: a manifest no encoder can satisfy is a 409 naming what it cannot do
steps.assert: the status and the error code

steps.expect: a codec name that does not exist is a 400 before ffmpeg
steps.assert: the status

steps.expect: capabilities report accepted and rejected families and subtitle_ocr_enabled agrees with the subtitle phase
steps.assert: the shape, and that subtitle_ocr_enabled matches what Phase 4 observed

steps.expect: a burst is 200, 200, 429 with Retry-After, health untouched, and the counter increments
steps.assert: the three statuses, the header, and astraeus_rate_limited_total

phases.title: Access, when a gate is configured

steps.expect: no token is a 401 and the right token is a 200; health needs no token
steps.assert: both statuses and an unauthenticated /api/health

steps.expect: a granted identity sees one library and the other answers 404, not 403
steps.assert: the counts and the 404

steps.expect: a non-admin gets 403 registering a library and on scan; an admin without visibility can still scan
steps.assert: both statuses, both directions

steps.expect: revoking a library stops its session URLs being served
steps.assert: the status changes after revocation

phases.title: Deployment, if you are checking a release

steps.expect: health answers and one entity plays against the built image or the installed unit
steps.assert: health and a successful playback

steps.expect: systemd-analyze security reports the score the runbook quotes
steps.why: provisioning a VM is outside what this walk-through drives

phases.note: the transcode half needs real media, but the point of this phase is the deployed artefact; it is marked human rather than given a fixture

notCovered: what is composited into a frame after a burn or an OCR pass - a browser cannot be asked, and the Go integration tests assert pixels instead
hardware encoders - no GPU on this host, so the walk-through asserts the reported reasons rather than the encoders
Firefox and Safari - not installed; the harnesses are Chromium-only and native HLS has never been observed firing
